correctness.rationale: Exact affine gradient steps give closed stationary moments under the stated strict common mean-square stability condition. The algebraic ratio identity reduces the comparison to a quartic P, and its transformed coefficient sign structure gives an at-most-two-root bound. A rational Sturm certificate for the degree-seven discriminant isolates the unique active transition. Rational roots in two parameter regimes show the count changes from two to zero at a double root; direct endpoint signs fix the ordering. Exact rational sample and reproducible symbolic checks corroborate the algebra. No finite experiment is used as a replacement for infinite root classification.

originality.rationale: Directly compared exact stationary last-iterate implications with the published common-Hessian exact model (Ying et al. 2018), a shared-Hessian noise approximation (Domingo-Enrich 2022), generic reshuffling counterexamples (De Sa 2020), epoch-rate comparisons (Safran and Shamir 2021), and averaged-iterate convergence bounds (Liu 2026). Related older specialist material could still contain an equivalent result.

value.rationale: The phenomenon addresses a genuine sampling-order decision: two strictly convex components whose exact-gradient noise differs by state can make reshuffling inferior at some constant steps, yet superior again near the stability boundary. The entire 2D parameter-region partition, unique algebraic curvature-ratio cutoff, and explicit rational witness are structural statements, beyond a qualitative counterexample or a small numerical improvement. The precise threshold can benchmark approximations and guide safe large-step comparisons.
